sentences.text: 5. It may be mentioned that the land was acquired for the public purpose of construction of bye-pass on Sonepat-Rathdhana Road leading to Meerut  Sonepat road.

6. The short question that falls for consideration is as to  3 what amount of compensation the aggrieved land owners are entitled to?
7.

Some of the undisputed facts that have emerged during the course of hearing are that a big chunk of land of village Patti Musalmanan, in Tehsil and District Sonepat, was acquired vide Notification dated 17.05.1990, issued under Section 4 of the Act.

In that case, the Reference Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.125/- per square yard for the land behind ECE factory situated away and on the left side of the Sonepat  Bahalgarh Road and Rs.150/- per square yard on the right side abutting the aforesaid road.

The High Court further enhanced the compensation from Rs.125/- to Rs.135/- for land on the left side and from Rs.150/- to Rs.160/- per square yard for the land on the right side on the principle applied by the Reference Court.

The matter eventually reached to this Court for further enhancement of compensation and vide judgment dated April 21, 2010 in Udho Dass vs. State of Haryana and Others, (2010) 12 SCC 51, this Court enhanced the compensation in the following terms:

sentences.text: In the case before us, admittedly the land was  acquired in the year 1990, had great potential  value, and has been completely urbanised as huge  residential complexes, industrial areas and estates  and a huge education city have come up in the last  ten or fifteen years.

Moreover, insofar land which  is to be used for residential purposes is concerned,
 a plot away from the main road is often of more  value, as the noise and the air pollution alongside  the arterial roads is almost unbearable.

It is also  significant that the land of Jamalpur Kalan was  touching the rear side of the ECE factory and the  High Court had granted compensation of Rs.250/- per  square yard for the acquisition of the year 1992.
We  have also seen the site plan to satisfy ourselves  4  and find that the land acquired from Jamalpur Kalan  and the present land share a common boundary behind  the ECE factory.
The belting system in the facts of  the present case
would thus not be permissible.

25 . We are, therefore, of the opinion as the said  award pertained to the year 1992, a sum of Rs.225/-
 per square yard which would come to Rs.10,89,000/-
 per acre would be the adequate compensation in the  present case and for arriving at this figure not  only have we computed the value of the land on the  date of the notification under Section 4 but have  also recognized its potential on the basis of  evidence of development in the area around the  Bahalgarh-Sonepat Road.
8.

Reverting back to the facts of the case in hand, it may be mentioned that prior to the subject acquisition proposed on 16.05.1996/16.07.1996, the land of village Kabirpur was acquired earlier also by the State of Haryana through the acquisition initiated vide Notification dated 17.05.1990 issued under Section 4 of the Act.

The public purpose of the said acquisition was same as was in Udho Dasss case(supra), namely, development of residential and commercial area in Sector  12, Sonepat.
9.

followed the decision of this Court in Udho Dass case (Supra) and,
consequently, granted compensation at the rate of Rs.225/- per square yard to the land owners of village Kabirpur.

sentences.text: 10. As noticed earlier, the acquisition in the instant case took place after six years i.e. on 16.05.1996/16.07.1996 when a proposal to acquire the land was notified under Section 4 of the Act.

In other words, the land owners of village Kabirpur, whose  5 lands were acquired in the year 1990, have been granted compensation at the rate of Rs.225/- per square yard, and that judgment has attained finality.

11. On the other hand, the appellants, whose lands we acquired six years later, have been granted compensation at the rate of Rs.120/- per square yard vide the impugned judgments dated 08.10.2009 and 20.09.2010.
12. In our considered view, the acquisition of t appellants land being later in time, they are entitled t compensation higher than the rate of Rs.225/- per square yard.

Ordinarily, this Court would have applied the principle of 12%
annual appreciation, however, the acquisition in the instant case being of two small parcels of land, we are satisfied that the ends of justice would be adequately met if the appellants are granted compensation at the rate of Rs.250/- per square yard, besides other statutory benefits as admissible under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894.
Ordered accordingly.
